context.title: When a flight changes, what a travel seller can do depends on the airline, and the dashboard doesn't say
context.body: Duffel notifies sellers of airline-initiated changes from 300+ airlines. For 20+ of them, the seller can accept the change straight away; for one, it can be automated; for the rest, someone has to review options with the customer, and customer-requested changes go to help@duffel.com by email. Each seller has to learn which path applies, while the flight's departure gets closer. The Duffel Assistant already hands travellers to support when it can't act; the seller's side deserves the same clarity.
assumptions: I haven't used the Duffel Dashboard. My view comes from Duffel's docs, help centre, blog and changelog, so some of this may have changed since those were written.
The concept assumes Duffel knows, per airline and change, whether it can be accepted in Duffel, needs support, or needs no action, which its docs imply.
The 4-hour support reply time is a proposal, not a published commitment.
Visual language from duffel.com: deep purple-black ink (#100024), teal and mint accents, zinc greys and GT America (Inter as substitute). No Duffel logo.
The seller, passengers and flights are fictional.

goals.title: Know what you can do
goals.body: Every change says whether you can resolve it here, need Duffel support, or can ignore it.

goals.title: Act before departure
goals.body: Sort by how soon the flight leaves, so urgent changes come first.

goals.title: Hand over without email
goals.body: When the Assistant can't act, send support a pre-filled request with the traveller's choice, and track the reply.

jtbd: When an airline changes my customer's flight, I want to know straight away whether I can fix it myself and how urgent it is, so the traveller gets a clear answer before they leave for the airport.

evidence.step: Changes come from hundreds of airlines
evidence.finding: Duffel notifies sellers of airline-initiated changes from 300+ connected airlines, via API, dashboard and email.

source.label: Duffel blog: Manage flight changes in minutes

evidence.step: Few can be resolved in one click
evidence.finding: Sellers can accept changes immediately for 20+ airlines and automate them for one; for hundreds more they only get notifications.

source.label: Duffel blog: Manage flight changes in minutes

evidence.finding: Duffel's help centre says flight changes are currently manual: non-IATA sellers email help@duffel.com, and changes can't be made through the API or dashboard.

source.label: Duffel Help: How do I change a customer's flight?

evidence.step: The Assistant hands over when it can't act
evidence.finding: The Duffel Assistant connects travellers to Duffel's support specialists where an automated action isn't available, and accepts a summary so agents have context.

source.label: Duffel Docs: Integrating the Duffel Assistant

evidence.finding: Duffel added an 'Action required' tab for airline changes awaiting a decision, first for British Airways orders, showing exactly what changed.

source.label: Duffel changelog: Resolve airline-initiated changes in the dashboard

evidence.step: The role is about disruption and AI
evidence.finding: The role owns Duffel's AI support product end to end, including 'when it hands over to a human, and how users understand, trust and correct it'.

approaches: Extend the Action required tab to every airline
Label each change by what the seller can do
Sort changes by time to departure
Draft the customer message with the Assistant
Replace support emails with a pre-filled, tracked request

ranges.title: Action required, everywhere
ranges.summary: Extend the Orders 'Action required' tab to every airline that supports changes.
cons: Unsupported airlines still arrive by email.

screens.alt: Sketch: Action required tab in Orders

ranges.title: Label by what you can do
ranges.summary: One queue that labels each change as accept here, needs support, or no action.
cons: No help writing to the traveller.

ranges.title: Change Desk
ranges.summary: A queue sorted by departure and labelled by action, with a was/now view, an Assistant-drafted message, one-click accept, and a pre-filled support hand-off tracked in place.
pros: Covers every path, not just supported airlines.
Same handover model the Assistant uses for travellers.
cons: Support SLAs need agreeing with operations.

screens.alt: Sketch: change detail with one-click accept
screens.label: Accept

decision.title: Change Desk: one queue, clear paths, handover built in
decision.body: Range 3. Changes sorted by departure and labelled by what the seller can do, with one-click accept where airlines allow it, an Assistant-drafted message, and a pre-filled, tracked hand-off to support where they don't.
reasons: Only 20+ of 300+ airlines can be resolved in one click, so the hard cases are the common ones.
Sorting by departure puts the 38-hour cancellation above the 10-day aircraft swap.
It mirrors the Assistant's traveller handover, so B2B and B2C feel like one product.
decision.tradeoff: A pre-filled request makes it easier to send things to support, which could raise volume. I'd measure it against fewer back-and-forth emails per case.

effortImpact.option: Label by what you can do

depth.body: Built in Duffel's visual language. Three moments: a queue of four changes sorted by departure, labelled 'Accept in Duffel', 'Needs Duffel support' or 'No action needed'; accepting BA's 2h10m delay with an Assistant-drafted message to the traveller; and handing Iberia's cancellation to Duffel's travel support with the traveller's chosen alternative, tracked with a reply time. The detail panel eases in, and motion turns off for people who reduce it. The seller, passengers and flights are fictional.

validation.method: I'd start with support tickets about airline changes and time-to-resolution data, then test Change Desk with travel sellers during a disruption-heavy week.
hypotheses: Sellers resolve supported changes faster when the path is labelled.
Pre-filled hand-offs need fewer follow-up messages than emails.
Fewer travellers arrive at the airport without knowing about a change.

metrics.name: Time to resolve
metrics.definition: Median hours from change detected to resolved, by path.

metrics.name: Messages per hand-off
metrics.definition: Back-and-forth messages per support case about a change.

metrics.name: Resolved before departure
metrics.definition: Share of actionable changes resolved more than 24h before departure.

nextSteps: Map which airlines and change types fall into each path today.
Review support tickets and emails about changes with operations.
Test the queue and hand-off with travel sellers in a busy disruption week.
Align the seller hand-off with the Assistant's traveller hand-off.
